sources.title: Indications of a spatial variation of the fine structure constant

evidence.text: Voigt-profile fitting with vpfit minimizes χ² simultaneously across species. Related redshifts and broadening parameters are tied; thermal and turbulent limiting models are likelihood-weighted. Velocity structure is finalized before introducing Δα/α as a free parameter; isotopic and hyperfine structure are included where available and appropriate.

sources.title: Spatial variation in the fine-structure constant -- new results from VLT/UVES

evidence.text: Thermal and turbulent fits are combined by matching the first two moments of a two-Gaussian mixture, weighted by exp(−AICC/2). Comparable fits with discrepant Δα/α values increase the resulting uncertainty through a between-model variance term.

sources.title: Subaru Telescope limits on cosmological variations in the fine-structure constant

evidence.text: Blinded spectra are fitted with multicomponent Voigt profiles using nonlinear χ² minimization. Models are trialled at Δα/α = 0 and selected by minimum reduced χ². After unblinding, velocity structure is held fixed in form; Δα/α is then freed while component parameters are reoptimized.

sources.title: Four direct measurements of the fine-structure constant 13 billion years ago

evidence.text: Apply the Many Multiplet Method through ω_z=ω_0+q[(α_z/α_0)²−1], fitting transitions with different sensitivity coefficients and signs. Laboratory wavelengths and atomic coefficients are taken from a cited compilation; their numerical accuracy is not independently assessed here.

sources.title: A new era of fine structure constant measurements at high redshift

evidence.text: Five regional best-fit models seed a VPFIT reoptimization with separate α parameters for individual components or small groups. Weak or blended components are grouped to give 47 estimates. Least trimmed squares removes 15% in each region, leaving 40 estimates.

sources.title: Further constraints on variation of the fine structure constant from alkali doublet QSO absorption lines

evidence.text: Modified vpfit performs simultaneous χ² minimization of multiple-component Voigt profiles. Each velocity component has column density N, Doppler width b and redshift z, with Δα/α added as a fit parameter. Transition shifts use the imported atomic relation ωz = ω0 + q1x + q2y.

sources.title: Limits on the dependence of the fine-structure constant on gravitational potential from white-dwarf spectra

evidence.text: Transition sensitivities q are computed from spectra at x=−0.01, 0 and +0.01 using configuration interaction plus many-body perturbation theory. The construction uses a Dirac–Fock VN potential, B-spline orbitals and excitations from 3dn, 3dn−1 4s and 3dn−1 4p, with n=4 for Fe V and n=6 for Ni V.

sources.title: Search for a Variation of the Fine Structure Constant around the Supermassive Black Hole in Our Galactic Center

evidence.text: Atomic sensitivity coefficients are calculated with AMBiT by varying α in flat-spacetime Dirac calculations. Configuration interaction treats valence correlations, augmented where applicable by many-body perturbation theory for core–valence correlations. Sodium uses a correlation-potential/Brueckner-orbital treatment instead.

sources.title: Limits on the dependence of the fine-structure constant on gravitational potential from white-dwarf spectra

evidence.text: A linear fit of fractional wavelength shifts against relative sensitivities Qα separates a common redshift intercept from an α-dependent slope. Separate Fe V and Ni V estimates are reported using selected transitions with usable laboratory wavelengths and identifiable calculated levels.

sources.title: Limits on the dependence of the fine-structure constant on gravitational potential from white-dwarf spectra

evidence.text: To test sensitivity to gain calibration, the authors fit and subtract a linear dependence of fractional wavelength shift on laboratory wavelength, then refit against Qα. This diagnostic can remove part of a genuine α signal as well as calibration contamination.

sources.title: Search for a Variation of the Fine Structure Constant around the Supermassive Black Hole in Our Galactic Center

evidence.text: Gaussian fits determine central wavelengths of strong, sufficiently isolated absorption lines; Monte Carlo simulations estimate their uncertainties. The analysis uses three lines per NIFS spectrum, six with IRCS and ten with NIRSPEC, referenced to experimental laboratory wavelengths.

sources.title: Search for a Variation of the Fine Structure Constant around the Supermassive Black Hole in Our Galactic Center

evidence.text: Bayesian inference with MULTINEST estimates Δα/α and redshift parameters. All epochs are fitted simultaneously, while separate instrument/filter offsets accommodate different wavelength solutions. Atomic sensitivity uncertainties enter the inference as nuisance-parameter priors.

evidence.text: Frequency ratios obey ΔR/R=(Kµ,1−Kµ,2)Δµ/µ. Adopted sensitivities are Kµ=0 for optical electronic transitions, −1/2 for molecular vibrational transitions and −1 for microwave hyperfine transitions.

evidence.text: The adopted rate approximation is λ ∝ G_F² Q_β³ m_e². Isolating variation of the Coulomb contribution gives the quoted sensitivity Δλ/λ ≈ 2×10⁴ Δα/α, which converts a decay-rate difference into an α constraint.

sources.title: Constraints on the variations of the fundamental couplings

evidence.text: Analyze α-decay through Coulomb-barrier penetration and β-decay through phase-space sensitivity, restricting detailed treatment to allowed and first-forbidden transitions. Meteoritic Re–Os isochrons and other chronometers supply the adopted lifetime precision; for 187Re the rate is approximated by λ ∝ G_F²Q_β³m_e².

sources.title: The Oklo bound on the time variation of the fine structure constant revisited

evidence.text: Differentiate nuclear energies with respect to the electromagnetic coupling at fixed nuclear Hamiltonian, approximate Coulomb energies semiclassically, and relate the response to optical isotope-shift charge-radius measurements through an electrostatic inequality and a uniform-sphere potential approximation.

sources.title: A Re-examination of the Re-187 bound on the variation of fundamental couplings

evidence.text: The isochron relates present daughter abundance to parent abundance through (¹⁸⁷Os) = (¹⁸⁷Os)_i + (¹⁸⁷Re)[exp(λt) − 1]. An independently known age converts the fitted slope into a decay constant; for varying λ, this inferred constant represents its time average.

sources.title: A Re-examination of the Re-187 bound on the variation of fundamental couplings

evidence.text: The numerical comparison uses meteoritic λ = (1.666 ± 0.009)×10⁻¹¹ yr⁻¹ and laboratory λ_0 = (1.639 ± 0.025)×10⁻¹¹ yr⁻¹. The resulting uncertainty is dominated by laboratory precision rather than the smaller meteoritic uncertainty.

sources.title: Constraints on the variations of the fundamental couplings

evidence.text: Use renormalization-group dimensional transmutation to relate coupling variations to Λ_QCD and the Higgs expectation value. Estimate heavy-nucleus Q-value sensitivities with a semi-empirical binding formula and Fermi-gas kinetic and potential contributions.

sources.title: Testing the neutrality of matter by acoustic means in a spherical resonator

evidence.text: Polarization calibrations use either an ac drive at resonance plus a dc offset, producing a response linear in the offset, or an ac drive at half the resonance frequency, producing a quadratic response in ac amplitude. sources.title: Testing the neutrality of matter by acoustic means in a spherical resonator

evidence.text: The authors derive an inhomogeneous acoustic wave equation from linearized fluid motion and mass conservation. Separation into spherical harmonics and spherical Bessel functions determines the rigid-wall spectrum; driven solutions use force-dependent boundary conditions and numerical integration.

sources.title: Testing the neutrality of matter by acoustic means in a spherical resonator

evidence.text: Neutrality is inferred from intercepts of polarization-versus-dc-voltage regressions. Point uncertainties are chosen to give reduced χ² near unity. Positive- and negative-dc subsets are averaged separately, then half-summed to remove an observed sign-reversing contribution.

sources.title: A bound on the 12C/13C ratio in near-pristine gas with ESPRESSO

evidence.text: Isotope-limit calibration generates mock C II profiles from the best-fitting model, varies 12C/13C at fixed total C II column, and applies 500 error-spectrum noise realizations per input ratio. Recovered-ratio distributions determine the confidence bound.

sources.title: Does the fine structure constant vary? A Detailed investigation into systematic effects

evidence.text: Refit Mg and Si transitions using only ²⁴Mg and ²⁸Si, setting ²⁵,²⁶Mg and ²⁹,³⁰Si abundances to zero. The authors use this extreme depletion scenario as an upper-limit test of the proposed isotopic-evolution effect.

sources.title: Revision of VLT/UVES constraints on a varying fine-structure constant

evidence.text: Fits multicomponent Voigt profiles with vpfit, varying Δα/α simultaneously with nuisance parameters. The relative stopping tolerance is Δχ²tol/χ²=2×10⁻⁷. Errors derive from the covariance matrix and are increased for elevated reduced χ²; external-parameter χ² scans provide a consistency comparison.

sources.title: Evidence for time variation of the fine structure constant

evidence.text: Each system receives 150 trial-α fits in each of the three width treatments. Formal 1σ intervals use a unit change from minimum χ². Acceptance requires statistically acceptable individual spectral regions and agreement among all three α estimates within 1σ; about one tenth of the sample is rejected. The accepted estimate uses the smallest of the three χ² minima.

sources.title: A bound on the 12C/13C ratio in near-pristine gas with ESPRESSO

evidence.text: Joint χ² minimization with alis uses single-component Voigt profiles. ESPRESSO anchors the redshift; archival features receive independent velocity offsets. Continuum fits use third-order Legendre polynomials, with a fitted common ESPRESSO zero-level and wavelength-dependent instrumental widths.

sources.title: A bound on the 12C/13C ratio in near-pristine gas with ESPRESSO

evidence.text: Adopts a previously developed stochastic enrichment model: sample a power-law IMF normalized by the number of enriching stars, combine stellar yields, and evaluate [C/O], [Si/O], [Fe/O] and the isotope lower bound. emcee samples α, N_star, M_min and M_max.

sources.title: Prospects for detecting new dark physics with the next generation of atomic clocks

evidence.text: How sensitively can existing and near-future atomic and molecular clock comparisons constrain scalar-induced variations of the proton-to-electron mass ratio associated with modified gravity, dark energy and dark matter?

sources.title: Further evidence for cosmological evolution of the fine structure constant

evidence.text: Do quasar absorption spectra provide evidence that the fine structure constant differed from its present value, and can instrumental or astrophysical systematic effects explain the inferred shifts?

sources.title: Indications of a spatial variation of the fine structure constant

evidence.text: Do relative atomic absorption-line spacings in quasar spectra indicate spatial variation of the fine-structure constant, and can instrumental systematics explain the apparent dipole?

evidence.text: What limit on cosmological variation of low-energy α follows from a new many-multiplet analysis using an independent fitting code and a uniform, high-quality quasar absorption sample, with simulation-based controls on blending and weak lines?

sources.title: Subaru Telescope limits on cosmological variations in the fine-structure constant

evidence.text: Do independently calibrated Subaru quasar absorption spectra show cosmological variation of α, and do sight-lines nearer the proposed spatial dipole's anti-pole support that model once long-range wavelength distortions are addressed?

sources.title: Four direct measurements of the fine-structure constant 13 billion years ago

evidence.text: Do absorption systems toward the high-redshift quasar J1120+0641 show a change in α relative to Earth, and how do the new measurements affect a spatial-dipole fit when combined with earlier direct measurements?

sources.title: Further evidence for a variable fine-structure constant from Keck/HIRES QSO absorption spectra

evidence.text: Do relative shifts of QSO absorption transitions indicate variation of the fine-structure constant, and can instrumental or astrophysical systematic effects explain those shifts?

sources.title: Further constraints on variation of the fine structure constant from alkali doublet QSO absorption lines

evidence.text: What constraint on cosmological variation of α follows from improved Si IV alkali-doublet spectroscopy and laboratory wavelengths, and how sensitive is that constraint to instrumental and astrophysical systematic errors?

sources.title: Probing the cosmological variation of the fine - structure constant: Results based on VLT - UVES sample

evidence.text: Can an independently analyzed, homogeneous set of high-quality quasar absorption spectra constrain cosmological variation of α, while simulations guide selection against weak-line and velocity-blending systematics?

sources.title: The Oklo bound on the time variation of the fine structure constant revisited

evidence.text: What conservative constraint on a change in the fine-structure constant follows from Oklo rare-earth isotope data when reactor-temperature uncertainty and the nuclear response of the Sm149 capture resonance are treated explicitly?

sources.title: Limits on the dependence of the fine-structure constant on gravitational potential from white-dwarf spectra

evidence.text: Can metal absorption lines in a white-dwarf atmosphere constrain dependence of the fine-structure constant on gravitational environment, including scalar-mediated behavior inaccessible to small seasonal potential changes near Earth?

sources.title: A Re-examination of the Re-187 bound on the variation of fundamental couplings

evidence.text: What constraint on varying fundamental couplings follows from comparing meteoritic ¹⁸⁷Re decay with present laboratory measurements, once the interpretation of the meteoritic precision and the decay rate's time average is corrected?

sources.title: Search for a Variation of the Fine Structure Constant around the Supermassive Black Hole in Our Galactic Center

evidence.text: Can differential absorption-line spectroscopy of late-type stars near Sagittarius A* constrain a spatial difference in the fine-structure constant between the Galactic Center and Earth, including a possible dependence on gravitational potential?

sources.title: A new era of fine structure constant measurements at high redshift

evidence.text: What constraints on fine-structure constant variation follow from an LFC-calibrated quasar spectrum, and how do wavelength calibration, line broadening and component-level modelling affect the inferred result?

sources.title: Constraints on the variations of the fundamental couplings

evidence.text: How do correlated variations of gauge and Yukawa couplings, Λ_QCD and quark masses alter nuclear limits on fine-structure variation from Oklo, long-lived radioactive isotopes and stellar bound-state β-decays?

sources.title: Spatial variation in the fine-structure constant -- new results from VLT/UVES

evidence.text: Do quasar absorption spectra favor spatial or temporal variation of the fine-structure constant, and can instrumental or astrophysical effects explain the apparent variation?
